documents.title: John Doe
documents.content: Jordan faced academic challenges such as imposter syndrome and time management in the first semester, but adapted by regularly attending office hours and joining a peer study group. As a first‑generation student, Jordan experiences pride and pressure, balancing financial responsibilities with academic expectations. Faculty support is generally positive, but varies by class size; teaching assistants and small electives provide more personalized help. Jordan leveraged campus resources like career services and mental‑health counseling, noting both successes (internship) and delays (counseling appointments). Extracurricular involvement in the Computer Science Society and a coding outreach program helped Jordan develop leadership and communication skills. Jordan suggests institutional improvements: structured mentorship for first‑generation students, a unified information dashboard, and better coordination of major assessment deadlines.

documents.title: Imposter Syndrome & Confidence Building
documents.content: Feelings of inadequacy in early courses led to hesitation to ask questions; confidence grew through office hours, peer groups, and successful problem solving.

documents.title: Proactive Use of Campus Resources
documents.content: Jordan learned to navigate office hours, career services, scholarships, and mental‑health counseling, turning initially hidden resources into tools for academic and professional success.

documents.title: Need for Centralized Information & Mentorship
documents.content: Scattered communication and lack of structured support for first‑generation students create cognitive load; a unified dashboard and mentorship program are suggested.

documents.title: Workload Stress & Assessment Coordination
documents.content: Midterms, finals, and overlapping project deadlines cause spikes in stress; better inter‑departmental scheduling could alleviate pressure.

documents.title: Extracurricular Leadership Development
documents.content: Leadership roles in the CS Society and outreach volunteering enhanced communication, teamwork, and motivation.
